questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What is “carcinization”?
A. The development of cancer in organisms
B. The process of evolving into a crab-like form
C. The hardening of exoskeletons in arthropods
Answer: B. Carcinization is an example where different species can independently evolve similar traits, in this case, a crab-like body structure. One proposed advantage of the crab-like form is increased protection from predators. The broader, flatter body and reduced abdomen help crabs move more efficiently under rocks and in narrow crevices, providing better defense mechanisms.
questions.de: Wie heißt die konvergente Evolution, bei der Krebstiere, die keine Krabben sind, wiederholt einen krabbenartigen Körperbau entwickeln?
questions.en: What is the name for the convergent evolution in which non-crab crustaceans repeatedly evolve a crab-like body plan?

timeline.labelEn: Lancelot Borradaile introduces carcinization: “the many attempts of Nature to evolve a crab”
timeline.labelDe: Lancelot Borradaile führt die Karzinisierung ein: „die vielen Versuche der Natur, eine Krabbe zu entwickeln“

questions.cardText:
[Philosophy] Plato was a student of:
A. Aristotle B. Socrates C. Archimedes
Answer: B.
